source.title: RePlay: Retrieval-Based Voice Playback for Multi-Turn spoken dialogue
source.authors: Sathvik Udupa; Naveen Kumar; Ryan Folmsbee

record.tranche_reason: The study probes whether a hidden state in a spoken-dialogue model makes the upcoming response recoverable. This is a conceptual test of future-content decodability, using response-embedding retrieval rather than future-token prediction.
record.gate_note: The study reports probing results for an unmodified PersonaPlex checkpoint. It also reports retrieval performance for RePlay, whose retrieval head was trained for that task; those downstream system results do not isolate the original checkpoint's uninduced future-content representation and are not catalogued as rows.
record.test_reason: The study probes an unmodified PersonaPlex checkpoint, a full-duplex speech model, to see whether one hidden state at turn start encodes the upcoming response. That is future-content decodability in a new setting (speech dialogue). The target is a sentence embedding of the whole response, not specific tokens at fixed offsets, so it bears on V2 only loosely. T3 fits better than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the upcoming response becomes recoverable once the turn-start token is fed back as input. The authors exploit layer 15 for a truncated retrieval system.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses layer-wise probing of a spoken-dialogue model and predicts response embeddings rather than probing future text tokens; it compares the frame where the turn-start token is predicted with the frame where it is input.
record.method_sensitivity: The result differs between the <EPAD>predict and <EPAD>input frames and varies by layer; the reported rise is around layers 13–14, with layer 15 selected.
record.problems: The probing outcomes are described qualitatively in the text, while the figure's numerical values are unavailable in the supplied text. The probe recovers a response embedding, not future tokens at specified offsets. The paper notes that its evaluation relies on synthetic training data, an LLM judge, and a small user study; these limitations concern the broader system evaluation.
record.rows_left_out: RePlay's retrieval and dialogue-evaluation results, including Table 2 and Table 3, were omitted because its retrieval heads were trained for the retrieval task and those results do not isolate the unmodified model's future-content representation.

untested.parts: Prediction of specific future tokens at stated offsets; text-only LMs; how far ahead in tokens the information reaches.
All parts: no rhyming verse and no intervention.
All parts: no causal test of whether the features are computed for later positions.
All parts: no reasoning, chess or Sokoban tasks. Speech dialogue is probed only for decodability.
All parts: no test of whether the decodable representation steers generation.

missing.what: Near-chance probe accuracy at <EPAD>input for layers below about 13 (layer dependence of decodability)

record.verdict_notes: Changed the <EPAD>predict verdict from 'challenges' to 'limits_scope'. V2 does not specify which frame must carry the information, and the effect does appear one frame later in the same model. There is no explicit control for whether the probe decodes question content that determines the answer. The null at <EPAD>predict, where the question is also available, partly addresses this. The probe data are small (200/100 QA items), with no uncertainty reported. RePlay system results were rightly excluded as trained retrieval heads.

versions.untested_parts: No rhyming-verse task, candidate rhyme-word representation, or intervention changing an ending to test its effect on intermediate text.
The study probes recoverability of a spoken response embedding, not exact future tokens at specified offsets or several-token-ahead token prediction in a text-only language model.
No causal intervention establishes that the original model computes a feature for later positions rather than as a byproduct of next-token prediction.
No rhyme-planning test in smaller open-weight models.
No multi-step reasoning, chess, Sokoban, or comparable look-ahead task.
The study does not test whether the apparent representation is shallow, incidental, or causally irrelevant to intermediate generated text.

relation.reason: Section 3.2 reports original probes of PersonaPlex's upcoming response content before developing the retrieval system; the study does more than use a previously established finding.

tranche.reason: Original probing results examine upcoming response content in a new full-duplex speech setting, bearing on broader internal look-ahead beyond verse (V5). They do not directly test V2's future-token target.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased. Exact Figure 1 accuracies and numerical chance baselines are not stated in the supplied text; the rows correctly preserve qualitative results.

statements.correction: At <EPAD>input, probe performance rises sharply around layers 13–14 and improves thereafter; earlier-layer performance cannot be verified from the supplied figure text.

statements.correction: Response-embedding recovery succeeds at <EPAD>input after the layer-wise rise; probes remain near chance at <EPAD>predict; token-level V2 untested.
